name: cc-harness
description: cc-harness — a four-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer built on the one below. 1) cc-tools gives you the primitives and the house rules. 2) cc-pipeline is the build pipeline that carries a task from idea to hardened code. 3) cc-worker is the second pilot that drives the pipeline on one project. 4) cc-chief is the top brain that orchestrates workers across a product's sub-projects. Install cc-tools first.

plugins.name: cc-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/4 — primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you or the model reach for while working: /slap resets a stuck fix, /likec4 draws C4 architecture-as-code, /reminder pins one rule file as a hard constraint. Also ships the harness's rule files (rules/) to copy into a project's .claude/rules/. The primitives every layer above builds on.

plugins.name: cc-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/4 — the build pipeline. Five stage skills that carry one task from a decision to hardened code: /how-to-do (decide a fork), /do (build it by a tight set of writing rules), then /refactor, /review, /test to harden and ship it. Skills only. Built on cc-tools; driven by cc-worker.

plugins.name: cc-worker
plugins.description: Layer 3/4 — the second pilot. Hand /worker any piece of work (a fix, a change, a feature, a question) and it adapts: reads the goal (features) and design (architecture), then drives the right cc-pipeline and cc-tools skills to finish it. Runs inline as /worker or as a native subagent you delegate a whole task to. Also owns the features (/planner-brainstorm) and architecture (/sysdesign-brainstorm). Built on cc-pipeline + cc-tools.

plugins.name: cc-chief
plugins.description: Layer 4/4 — the top brain. /chief (backed by the chief-rules skill) orchestrates the workers across a product's sub-projects, each its own git repo under the current folder. It owns the product plane — the product-wide features of cross-cutting capabilities (features-management), direction finding (what-to-do), and the product CLAUDE.md (via /chief-init) — keeps each repo's features true, and sequences and dispatches workers (as native subagents) where cross-repo work needs them. It conducts; the workers build. Built on cc-worker.
